A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WildBench. Their main text, tables, equations, figures, and appendices are readable, including the image-based leaderboards, and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WildBench evaluations of 40 LLMs, task-category analyses, and correlations with human-based Chatbot Arena rankings.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds ablation findings and a September leaderboard containing 61 models.

M1.justification: Appendix F introduces and uses WB-Elo: WB-Reward and WB-Score are converted into pairwise comparisons for Elo updates starting from existing LMSYS ratings. This adds a substantive ranking procedure, although its implementation is only briefly described. The original two scoring methods remain.

E1.justification: Both versions describe the same 1,024-example WildBench V2 collection of English WildChat tasks, with the same task categories and conversation-history coverage. Additional illustrative queries and experimental controls do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The competing evaluation methods remain ArenaHard and AlpacaEval2 with raw and length-controlled win rates; the three WB-Reward reference LLMs also remain unchanged. The September leaderboard expands the evaluated LLM subjects. Newly cited TIGERScore and Prometheus are not reported as evaluated comparator metrics.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 61-model leaderboard evaluated with WB-Elo and experiments using checklist-removal controls, alternative judges, and additional length thresholds of 100, 200, and 1,000 characters. The original 14-model and top-six correlation analysis remains unchanged. Settings connecting the September scores to the June results are incompletely documented.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 tests checklist inclusion, sensitivity to five length-penalty thresholds, and judging with GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, and Mistral-Large. These substantially extend the earlier task-category analysis, length examples, and comparisons of penalties at 500 characters versus infinity, although several new findings are reported only qualitatively.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its original evaluations. The added ablations continue to report point estimates or qualitative findings without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 3 and the June leaderboard are retained. Section 4.3 adds checklist correlations of 0.905 without checklists and 0.925 with them, plus length-penalty and judge-choice findings. Figure 7 adds extensive September results, including GPT-4o's WB-Elo (LC) of 1227.1 and category scores for 61 models; these are additional results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The WB-Reward weights and WB-Score rescaling formula are unchanged. WB-Elo receives a procedural description, but no new formal mathematical specification, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: challenging real-user tasks, checklist-guided evaluation, two primary metrics, length-bias mitigation, and strong human-ranking correlations. The headline correlations of approximately 0.98 and 0.95 remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's limitations section, losing explicit caveats about API-mediated leakage, source-population biases, and GPT-4-generated conversation histories; English filtering remains documented elsewhere. It adds explanations of distribution mismatch, recommendations about judge choice and length penalties, and discussion of metric cost and personalization tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds manual-review criteria, reports approximately 10 minutes and $5 for WB-Score versus 3-4 times the cost for WB-Reward, and describes a supplementary archive containing code and data. It also corrects the documented individual-scoring prompt's output instructions to request strengths, weaknesses, and a rating. These disclosures do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for WildVision, TIGERScore, Prometheus 2, WildTeaming, and ZebraLogic, while removing the SEAL comparison. The central positioning against expert-curated benchmarks and other evaluations using real-user queries remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained, with targeted language corrections and expanded task and checklist explanations. v2 adds Section 4.3, removes the limitations section, reorders the appendices, and switches to author-year citations without extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds a comparative task-example figure, a boxed G20 checklist, and a September leaderboard with WB-Elo and task-category columns. It moves the evaluation-framework diagram from Figure 1 to Figure 4 and substantially reformats and reflows headings, tables, figures, and appendix prompt blocks. Existing distribution and radar plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer examples, corrected prompt instructions, and new ablations provide benefits. However, v2 removes important limitations, leaves WB-Elo insufficiently specified, and reports a checklist-enabled correlation of 0.925 without reconciling it with Table 3's retained WB-Score value of 0.940. These unresolved reporting issues limit the value of the additions, while the lost caveats weaken transparency, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
